questions.md:
Test for consistency and solve by Gauss elimination method

$$\begin{aligned} 3x + 4y - z - 6w &= 0 \\ 2x + 3y + 2z - 3w &= 0 \\ 2x + y - 145z - 9w &= 0 \\ x + 3y + 13z + 3w &= 0 \end{aligned}$$

Test for consistency and solve the following system of linear equations by Gauss elimination method.

$$\begin{aligned} 2x_1 + x_2 + 2x_3 + x_4 &= 6 \\ 6x_1 - 6x_2 + 6x_3 + 12x_4 &= 36 \\ 4x_1 + 3x_2 + 3x_3 - 3x_4 &= -1 \\ 2x_1 + 2x_2 - x_3 + x_4 &= 10 \end{aligned}$$

Test the consistency and hence solve by Gauss elimination method

$$\begin{aligned} x + 2y + z &= 2 \\ 3x + y - 2z &= 1 \\ 4x - 3y - z &= 3 \end{aligned}$$
Use Gram Schmidt orthogonalization process, to construct an orthonormal basis from the set of linearly independent vectors $\{a_1 = (1,1,1),\ a_2 = (1,-2,1),\ a_3 = (1,2,3)\}$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

Apply Gram Schmidt orthogonalization process to construct an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ from the following linearly independent set $S = \{a_1 = (-2,1,2),\ a_2 = (-7,2,1),\ a_3 = (-11,-11,-1)\}$.
Use Gram-Schmidt orthogonalization process to construct an orthonormal basis of $\mathbb{R}^3$ from the given set of vectors $\{(1,2,1), (2,3,4), (3,1,0)\}$
Use method of variation of parameters to solve $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + 4y = \tan 2x$
Use method of variation of parameter to solve $(D^2 - 3D + 2)y = \sin(e^{-x})$
Use method of variation of parameters to solve $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} + y = \sec x$

Use Gauss-Seidel method to solve the system of equations

$$\begin{aligned} x + 17y - 2z &= 48 \\ 30x - 2y + 3z &= 75 \\ 2x + 2y + 18z &= 30 \end{aligned}$$

Carry out 3 iterations and correct to 4 decimal places.

Use Gauss Seidel method to solve the system of linear equations:

$$\begin{aligned} 3x + y + z &= 9.3 \\ x - 2y + 10z &= 30.6 \\ 2x + 5y - z &= 10.5 \end{aligned}$$

Perform 3 iterations and correct the solution up to 4 decimals by taking the initial approximation as $x^{(0)} = 1,\ y^{(0)} = 2,\ z^{(0)} = 3$.

Use Gauss-Jacobi's method to find an approximate solution for the system of linear equations

$$\begin{aligned} 28x + 4y - z &= 32 \\ x + 3y + 10z &= 24 \\ 2x + 17y + 4z &= 35 \end{aligned}$$

Take the initial approximation as $x^{(0)} = y^{(0)} = z^{(0)} = 0$, carry out four iterations.

questions.md: Solve the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2y}{dt^2} + 2\dfrac{dy}{dt} + y = 6t\,e^{-t}$ given $y(0) = 0,\ y'(0) = 0$
Use Simpson's $\tfrac{3}{8}$th rule to find the area under the curve $y = \sqrt{x^2 + x + 1}$ between the ordinates $x = 1$ and $x = 2.2$. Take $h = 0.2$ and correct to 4 decimal places.

The following table gives the velocity of a particle at time $t$.

| $t$ (sec) | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 | 10 | 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $v$ (m/sec) | 4 | 6 | 16 | 34 | 60 | 94 | 136 |

Use appropriate numerical method to find the distance moved by the particle in 12 sec.
Use Simpson's $\tfrac{3}{8}$ rule to evaluate $\displaystyle\int_{0.2}^{1.4} (\sin x - \log x + e^x)\,dx$, by taking 6 sub-intervals.
Find all the eigenvalues and the eigenvector corresponding to the smallest eigenvalue of the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 2 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 3 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$.
Find all the eigenvalues and any two eigenvectors of the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$
Find all the eigenvalues and any two of the eigenvectors of the matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 & 3 \\ 1 & 5 & 1 \\ 3 & 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Using finite difference formula, find the value of $y(1991)$ and $y(2005)$ from the following table.

| $x$ | 1990 | 1993 | 1996 | 1999 | 2002 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $y$ | 110 | 90 | 101 | 98 | 89 |

The population of a town in the decennial census is given below. Use an appropriate interpolation formula to estimate the population for the year 1895.

| Year | 1891 | 1901 | 1911 | 1921 | 1931 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Population (in thousands) | 46 | 66 | 81 | 93 | 101 |

Use an appropriate interpolation formula to find an approximate value of $y(1)$ and $y''(8)$ from the following data:

| $x$ | 0 | 2 | 4 | 6 | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $y$ | 7 | 13 | 43 | 145 | 367 |

Prove that any subset $S$ of a linearly independent set $U$ of a vector space $V$ is linearly independent. Check whether or not the set of vectors $\{(1,1,0), (1,3,2), (4,9,5)\}$ from $\mathbb{R}^3$ is linearly independent.
Define maximal linearly independent subset of a vector space $V$ and prove that it forms a basis for $V$.
Test whether $B = \{(3,0,2), (7,0,9), (4,1,2)\}$ forms a basis for $\mathbb{R}^3$. If so, express $(1,2,3)$ in terms of basis vectors.
Diagonalize the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4 \\ 2 & 3 \end{pmatrix}$ and hence compute $A^5$.
Diagonalize the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 2 & 4 \end{pmatrix}$ and hence find $\sqrt{A}$.
Diagonalize the matrix $A = \begin{pmatrix} 5 & -3 \\ -6 & 2 \end{pmatrix}$. Hence, find $A^{10}$.
